checks.why: `axios.get('/api/items').then(renderItems)` is a request, not a registration: the path is the call's argument but nothing callable is handed to it, so renderItems (handed to .then) was labelled a GET route
`axios.post('/api/items', item)` hands over data (a parameter no declaration names), not a handler
`request.cookies.get('t')` has no path of its own: the '/login' on the line is redirect's argument, not get's
CONTROL: a router registration handing over a declared function is still a GET route
CONTROL: an inline arrow handler after middleware is still a POST route
CONTROL: `delete` is also Map.delete, and a router's delete handing over a declared function is still a route
CONTROL: a route written as one options object keeps its path, a property value inside the object
a `get` whose only argument is an object of data hands over nothing: readItem is not a GET route
CONTROL: a mock server's handler under a base-URL template keeps its route: the path is the template's own after `${...}`
`api.patch(`/users/profile`, data)` hands over a parameter that shares its name with another module's const: data, not a handler
